items.title: The Dirichlet series for zeta converges absolutely and locally uniformly on the half-plane Re s greater than 1
The Riemann zeta function on the half-plane Re s greater than 1
The Riemann zeta function has its Euler product on the half-plane Re s greater than 1
The Riemann zeta function has no zeros when Re s is greater than 1
The pole of zeta at 1 recovers Euclid's infinitude of primes without reminting it on this page
For Re s greater than 0, zeta admits the fractional-part integral formula with a simple residue-one pole at 1
items.strategy: Compare partial sums of the Dirichlet series with the integral of x^(-s) over unit intervals, rewrite the discrepancy using the fractional-part function, and use the uniform bound 0 <= {x} < 1 to obtain a holomorphic correction term on Re s > 0 together with the explicit pole 1/(s-1).

items.title: The Dirichlet eta series is holomorphic on Re s greater than 0 and equals the prefactor times zeta there
items.strategy: Start from the alternating regrouping on Re s > 1, continue both sides analytically to Re s > 0, and keep the result as a representation theorem so the proof never divides by 1-2^(1-s) at its zeros without a separate removability argument.

items.title: The Jacobi theta function theta(t)=sum over all integers of exp(-pi n squared t) for t greater than 0
The Jacobi theta function satisfies theta(t)=t to the minus one-half theta(1/t)
items.strategy: Use the fixed Fourier normalization under which the scaled Gaussian x -> exp(-pi t x^2) transforms to t^(-1/2) exp(-pi xi^2/t), then apply Poisson summation to the Gaussian. The notes record that the live FA prerequisite pages still have empty item lists on disk, so this local scaffold item remains the honest carrier of that seam for now.

items.title: The completed zeta function has its Mellin-theta integral representation on Re s greater than 1
items.strategy: Write (theta(t)-1)/2 as the positive series sum_{n>=1} exp(-pi n^2 t), justify Tonelli on Re s > 1, and evaluate each Mellin integral by the change of variables u = pi n^2 t to recover Gamma(s/2) n^(-s).

items.title: The completed zeta function Lambda(s)=pi to the minus s over 2 times Gamma(s over 2) times zeta(s)
The Riemann zeta function extends meromorphically to the complex plane with its only pole at 1
items.strategy: Start from the Mellin-theta representation on Re s > 1, split the integral at 1, use the theta transformation on the (0,1) piece, and isolate the polar terms 1/s and 1/(1-s). Solving back for zeta from Lambda then gives the unique meromorphic continuation with only the residue-one pole at s = 1.

items.title: The completed zeta function satisfies Lambda(s)=Lambda(1-s)
items.strategy: Use the split Mellin expression obtained from the theta integral and observe that after the change of variables t -> 1/t the transformed expression is symmetric under s -> 1-s. The same split formula also keeps the poles of Lambda at 0 and 1 explicit.

items.title: The Riemann zeta function satisfies the classical sine-gamma functional equation
items.strategy: Begin with Lambda(s)=Lambda(1-s) and then solve for zeta by applying the reflection and duplication formulas for Gamma so the completed-function symmetry becomes the classical sine-gamma identity for zeta.

items.title: The Riemann xi function xi(s)=one-half s(s-1)Lambda(s)
The Riemann xi function is entire of order one, real on the real axis, and symmetric under s to 1 minus s
items.strategy: Multiply the meromorphic completed zeta function by s(s-1)/2 to cancel the poles, inherit the symmetry from Lambda(s)=Lambda(1-s), and use Stirling's formula in the right half-plane together with symmetry across s -> 1-s to obtain the order-one growth bound.

items.title: The Riemann zeta function has no zeros on the closed half-plane Re s at least 1, except for its pole at 1
items.strategy: The Euler product gives zero-freeness on Re s > 1. On the boundary line Re s = 1 use the logarithm of the Euler product together with 3 + 4 cos theta + cos 2 theta = 2(1 + cos theta)^2 >= 0 and then let sigma -> 1+ to rule out a zero at 1 + it.

items.title: The only zeros of zeta on the nonpositive real axis are the negative even integers, and every other zero lies in the open critical strip
items.strategy: The sine factor in the classical functional equation produces zeros at the negative even integers, while the Gamma factor stays finite there. Zero-freeness on Re s >= 1 and symmetry under s -> 1-s and conjugation then force every remaining zero into the open strip 0 < Re s < 1.

items.title: The Riemann xi function has its genus-one Hadamard product over the nontrivial zeros of zeta
items.strategy: Apply the finite-order Hadamard factorization theorem to xi, whose order-one growth and entire continuation were just established, and write the result with the genus-one elementary factors E_1(s/rho) so the convergence prescription is explicit.

items.title: The Bernoulli numbers are defined by the generating series t over exp(t) minus 1
The Riemann zeta function has the standard Bernoulli special values at the positive even and nonpositive integers
items.strategy: Use the Bernoulli expansion of z/(e^z - 1) and the meromorphic continuation to read off the nonpositive integer values, then combine the classical functional equation with the sine product and the Gamma identities to derive the positive-even formula.

items.title: The analytic continuation of zeta is not the same object as the defining Dirichlet series outside Re s greater than 1
A short Euler-product truncation already numerically approximates zeta at 2
The special-value formula gives zeta(4)=pi to the fourth over 90
items.strategy: Expand t/(e^t-1) to read off B_4 = -1/30, then substitute m = 2 into the positive-even Bernoulli formula from the special-values theorem.

items.title: The functional equation gives zeta(0)=-1/2 without substituting into a zero-times-pole expression
Splitting the theta Mellin integral at 1 isolates the two polar terms of completed zeta
The functional equation shows that zeta(-2)=0 through the sine factor
Symmetric finite zero products model the genus-one product for xi
The eta series can represent the continued zeta function where the defining Dirichlet series diverges
The defining Dirichlet series for zeta diverges at s=1 because it becomes the harmonic series
FALSE: zeta is given by the same Dirichlet series for every complex s other than 1
FALSE: zeta(-1) is the ordinary sum 1+2+3 and so on
FALSE: the Riemann zeta function is entire
FALSE: the classical functional equation alone characterizes the Riemann zeta function
items.strategy: Multiply zeta by the nonconstant entire factor exp((s-1/2)^2), which is invariant under s -> 1-s. The modified function still satisfies the same functional equation, so that equation alone cannot characterize zeta.
